column3: NASB supplies “inclined.”
“Play the mourner” is rendered “pretend to be a mourner.”
“According to this word” is rendered “in this manner.”
The Hebrew reads “she said” (some manuscripts “she came”); NASB has “spoke.” “Save” is rendered “Help.”
“What is to you?” is rendered “What is your trouble?”, and NASB adds “for.”
“A deliverer” is rendered “no one to separate them.”
“Clan” is rendered “family,” and “not to establish” as “so as to leave … neither name nor remnant.”
“I will command on you” is rendered “I will give orders concerning you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The oath formula “if one hair will fall” is rendered as a negative (“not one hair … shall fall”); NASB adds “otherwise.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Plans plans” is rendered “plans ways.”
NASB adds “the reason … is because”; “word” is rendered “request.”
NASB supplies “who would destroy.”
“Become rest” is rendered “be comforting,” and “to hear good and bad” as “to discern good and evil.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “Indeed” and the emphatic “it was … who.”
“The face of the matter” is rendered “the appearance of things.”
The Hebrew “I do” is rendered “I will surely do.”
“Bowed down” is rendered “prostrated himself,” and “word” as “request.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“He will turn” is rendered as a command (“Let him turn”).
“Scalp” is rendered “crown of his head,” and “blemish” as “defect.”
“From the end of days to the days” is rendered “at the end of every year”; NASB places the explanation in parentheses.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Two years of days” is rendered “two full years.”
NASB supplies “for.”
“To my hand” is rendered “next to mine.”
